I'm pagan, a hard polytheist to be exact. I've been this for as long as I can remember although officially I grew up Catholic. Paganism and witchcraft have always felt very natural to me and I have a strongly animistic world view. I read Tarot cards, meditate, "commune" with plants and believe in spirits. I do magick, believe it works (am not sure how, but it does) and have a whole host of my own superstitions. A lot of people will probably scoff at me for it, and I'm totally cool with that because at the end of the day I've made peace with my own take on reality and other people's opinions don't affect that.

None of my friends have any idea. They're all the militantly atheist, scientific types who look down on things as innocuous as herbal teas. I used to suggest things I know work such as eating raw garlic to ward off a cold or comfrey to treat bruises, or apple cider vinegar to stimulate appetite--and have had my head bitten off by them because those things are "woo," not scientific thus not real. So now I don't say anything.

I blend in well because I am strongly against organized religion, and I'm critical of a lot of new age idiocy and am generally pro-science. But I straddle the science/spirituality divide and have beliefs that would make many neopagans uncomfortable, too.

Last week I was showing off my tattoo of Gemini and Orion on my shoulder and a friend's boyfriend asked if I was into astrology. Immediately my friend jumped to my defense say, "No, not her. Not at all. She would never be into any of that nonsense."

It made me laugh a little inside and then made me wonder at how poorly my friends truly know me.
I'm a pagan hippie in a sea of militant atheist friends.
